passages.text: On another day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came with them to present himself before Him.
passages.sermon:
The sons of God are heavenly beings.
They came to present themselves before the LORD.
Satan is an adversary.
Satan also came with the sons of God.
Satan came to present himself before the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיָּב֤וֹא גַֽם־ הַשָּׂטָן֙ בְּתֹכָ֔ם לְהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Where have you come from?” said the LORD to Satan. “From roaming through the earth,” he replied, “and walking back and forth in it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD asked Satan a question.
The LORD said, “Where have you come from?”
Satan answered the LORD.
Satan said, “I have been roaming through the earth.”
Satan said, “I have been walking back and forth in the earth.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּבֹ֑א וַיַּ֨עַן הַשָּׂטָ֤ן אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מִשֻּׁ֣ט בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּמֵהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still retains his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD asked Satan about Job.
Job is the LORD’s servant.
There is no one like Job on earth.
Job is blameless.
Job is upright.
Job fears God.
Job turns away from evil.
Job still holds firmly to his integrity.
Satan incited the LORD against Job.
The LORD acted against Job without cause.
Job remains faithful.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֗ן הֲשַׂ֣מְתָּ לִבְּךָ֮ אֶל־ עַבְדִּ֣י אִיּוֹב֒ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין כָּמֹ֜הוּ בָּאָ֗רֶץ אִ֣ישׁ תָּ֧ם וְיָשָׁ֛ר יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וְעֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּת֔וֹ וַתְּסִיתֵ֥נִי ב֖וֹ לְבַלְּע֥וֹ חִנָּֽם׃

passages.text: “Skin for skin!” Satan replied. “A man will give up all he owns in exchange for his life.
passages.sermon: Satan spoke to the LORD.\r\nSatan said, “Skin for skin!”\r\nA man will give everything he has to save his own life.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן הַשָּׂטָ֛ן אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר ע֣וֹר בְּעַד־ ע֗וֹר וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָאִ֔ישׁ יִתֵּ֖ן בְּעַ֥ד נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: But stretch out Your hand and strike his flesh and bones, and he will surely curse You to Your face.”
passages.sermon:
Satan spoke to the LORD.
Satan challenged God.
Satan said, “Reach out Your hand.
Strike Job’s body.
Strike his flesh and bones.
If You do this, Job will curse You to Your face.”
passages.original: אוּלָם֙ שְֽׁלַֽח־ נָ֣א יָֽדְךָ֔ וְגַ֥ע אֶל־ עַצְמ֖וֹ וְאֶל־ בְּשָׂר֑וֹ אִם־ לֹ֥א אֶל־ פָּנֶ֖יךָ יְבָרֲכֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: “Very well,” said the LORD to Satan. “He is in your hands, but you must spare his life.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Satan.
The LORD gave Satan permission to act against Job.
The LORD said, "Job is in your hands."
The LORD commanded, "You must protect his life."
The LORD did not allow Satan to kill Job.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ הַשָּׂטָ֖ן הִנּ֣וֹ בְיָדֶ֑ךָ אַ֖ךְ אֶת־ נַפְשׁ֥וֹ שְׁמֹֽר׃

passages.text: So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and infected Job with terrible boils from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
passages.sermon:
Satan left the presence of the LORD.
Satan attacked Job.
Satan gave Job terrible boils.
The boils covered Job’s body.
The boils went from the soles of Job’s feet to the crown of his head.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵא֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־ אִיּוֹב֙ בִּשְׁחִ֣ין רָ֔ע מִכַּ֥ף רַגְל֖וֹ עַד קָדְקֳדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself as he sat among the ashes.
passages.sermon:
Job suffered greatly.
He had painful boils all over his body.
Job took a piece of broken pottery.
He used the pottery to scrape his skin.
Job sat among the ashes.
passages.original: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ ל֣וֹ חֶ֔רֶשׂ לְהִתְגָּרֵ֖ד בּ֑וֹ וְה֖וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּתוֹךְ־ הָאֵֽפֶר׃

passages.text: Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
passages.sermon:
Job’s wife spoke to him.
She saw Job suffering.
She asked Job a question.
She said, “Do you still hold on to your integrity?”
She told Job, “Curse God and die.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ עֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּתֶ֑ךָ בָּרֵ֥ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֻֽת׃

passages.text: “You speak as a foolish woman speaks,” he told her. “Should we accept from God only good and not adversity?” In all this, Job did not sin in what he said.
passages.sermon:
Job was a righteous man.
Job suffered greatly.
Job’s wife spoke to him.
She told Job to curse God and die.
Job replied to his wife.
He said, “You speak like a foolish woman.”
He asked her a question.
He said, “Should we accept good from God and not accept trouble?”
Job did not sin with his words.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כְּדַבֵּ֞ר אַחַ֤ת הַנְּבָלוֹת֙ תְּדַבֵּ֔רִי גַּ֣ם אֶת־ הַטּ֗וֹב נְקַבֵּל֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאֶת־ הָרָ֖ע לֹ֣א נְקַבֵּ֑ל בְּכָל־ זֹ֛את לֹא־ חָטָ֥א אִיּ֖וֹב בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: Now when Job’s three friends—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite—heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, each of them came from his home, and they met together to go and sympathize with Job and comfort him.
passages.sermon:
Job had three friends.
Their names were Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite.
They heard about all the adversity that had come upon Job.
Each friend came from his own home.
They met together.
They decided to go to Job.
They wanted to sympathize with him.
They wanted to comfort him.
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֞וּ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת׀ רֵעֵ֣י אִיּ֗וֹב אֵ֣ת כָּל־ הָרָעָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֮ הַבָּ֣אָה עָלָיו֒ וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ אֱלִיפַ֤ז הַתֵּימָנִי֙ וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֔י וְצוֹפַ֖ר הַנַּֽעֲמָתִ֑י וַיִּוָּעֲד֣וּ יַחְדָּ֔ו לָב֥וֹא לָנֽוּד־ ל֖וֹ וּֽלְנַחֲמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When they lifted up their eyes from afar, they could barely recognize Job. They began to weep aloud, and each man tore his robe and threw dust in the air over his head.
passages.sermon:
Job’s three friends came to see him.
They looked at Job from far away.
They could barely recognize Job.
They began to weep loudly.
Each man tore his own robe.
Each man threw dust into the air over his head.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂא֨וּ אֶת־ עֵינֵיהֶ֤ם מֵרָחוֹק֙ וְלֹ֣א הִכִּירֻ֔הוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם וַיִּבְכּ֑וּ וַֽיִּקְרְעוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מְעִל֔וֹ וַיִּזְרְק֥וּ עָפָ֛ר עַל־ רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם הַשָּׁמָֽיְמָה׃

passages.text: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, but no one spoke a word to him because they saw how intense his suffering was.
passages.sermon:
Job suffered greatly.
Three friends came to visit Job.
Their names were Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar.
They sat on the ground with Job.
They stayed with him for seven days.
They stayed with him for seven nights.
No one spoke to Job.
They saw that Job’s pain was very great.
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁב֤וּ אִתּוֹ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים וְשִׁבְעַ֣ת לֵיל֑וֹת וְאֵין־ דֹּבֵ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי־ גָדַ֥ל הַכְּאֵ֖ב מְאֹֽד׃
